projects.title: Foundational Axiom Identification in Reasoning Systems

review.alternative: Implicit single-prompt mixing of cognition and control can sometimes match task success metrics without explicit separation.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing prompt-based monolithic models achieving higher auditability and lower unsupported assertions than decoupled architectures.

claims.statement: Architectural separation of cognition, control, and memory makes the justificatory basis of AI decisions explicit, enabling better auditability.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that decoupling cognition and control improves justificatory clarity.
support.passage: The Structured Cognitive Loop (SCL) is introduced as an architectural alternative that separates these functions. In SCL, the language model is dedicated to cognition only, execution is governed by a lightweight controller that mediates every proposal before any action is taken, and memory is maintained externally as a structured store of verified facts.

actions.findings: Architectural separation of cognition, control, and memory makes the justificatory basis of AI decisions explicit, enabling better auditability. [source-51196608d740480b]
actions.limitations: Sustaining uncertainty risks decision paralysis in time-sensitive environments. Current implementation models for CD-AI are primarily theoretical and lack large-scale benchmarks compared to standard RLHF baselines.
actions.next_questions: How can PCFG-derived uncertainty metrics be integrated directly into control loops to autonomously trigger meta-reasoning?
actions.reason: Revising the notebook incorporating new source evidence on flow states and system validation to support the foundational assumption challenge project.
actions.summary: Foundational reasoning axioms are best challenged through architectural separation (decoupling cognition from control) and the deliberate inclusion of dissonance to prevent premature closure on unverified truths.
actions.title: Architectural and Methodological Paths to Reasoning Transparency

proposal.summary: This cycle reviews structural methods for testing foundational assumptions in intelligent systems, focusing on how architectural separation and cognitive dissonance frameworks manage uncertainty.
proposal.title: Journal Entry: Cycle 11 Synthesis on Foundational Assumptions and Reasoning Systems
